messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH - embeddings-service p95 token latency > 2s in us-west-2. Trigger: embeddings.token_latency.p95 > 2s for 3min. Pager: @oncall-rotation

meenakshi: acknowledging, jumping on bridge. seeing customer 503s in grafana. spawning bridge now :rotating_light:

vikram: +1 on bridge. quick hypothesis: downstream kv-cache eviction spike after last rollout? saw a queue backlog on redis-x.

lucas: Customer Ops already got two tickets from an enterprise customer complaining about slow responses. marking high-impact.

jen: product: any degradations to user-visible endpoints? embeddings are used by search ranking for prod customers. Need impact estimate.

meenakshi: initial tail-latency spike correlates with a flurry of small batches at 16 tokens causing poor batching efficiency. also a few nodes in the pool showing high CPU.

vikram: running quick check:
```
# check pod restarts and cpu
kubectl get pods -l app=embeddings -o wide
kubectl logs -f embeddings-xyz -c runtime | tail -n 200
```

vikram: logs show repeated `KVCache: eviction miss` and `batcher: flush_due_to_timeout` spam. suspect kv cache TTL misconfig after the config push at 08:14 UTC.

meenakshi: rolling back the TTL change on canary to see if it stabilizes. initiating immediate rollback on canary nodes.

oncall-rotation: ack, taking bridge lead for now. tagging incident as customer-impact > 1 customer.

lucas: posted update to affected customer with ETA 30m. keeping them updated.

sara: FYI I muted some low-value alerts to reduce noise while we focus. I silenced `batcher.flush.warn` for 15m (reason: known noise).

vikram: rollback done on canary (08:24 UTC). monitoring p95.

meenakshi: p95 trending down to ~1.1s now. errors dropping. keeping bridge open for 20m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: auto-suppression engaged for repeated alerts from `batcher.flush_due_to_timeout` (rule: dedupe:5m).

jen: thanks. we should schedule a post-incident to capture root cause and fix plan. can we get a short timeline and action items here?

vikram: quick timeline:
- 08:12 UTC: config push (kv-cache ttl) to embeddings canary
- 08:14 UTC: first spike in eviction logs
- 08:16 UTC: alert fired (p95 > 2s)
- 08:18 UTC: bridge created, rollback started
- 08:24 UTC: rollback completed, p95 improving
- 08:40 UTC: stable under threshold

meenakshi: proposed action items:
1) Reproduce TTL change in staging with load test (owner: vikram)
2) Add a circuit-breaker metric on kv-cache eviction rate with paging threshold (owner: sara)
3) Revise alerting: make `batcher.flush` a warning-only alert and create a new `embeddings.customer-impact` alert that triggers paging only when both p95 > threshold AND error-rate > X (owner: oncall-rotation)
4) Postmortem doc and exec summary (owner: jen)
5) Communicate RCA and mitigation to affected customers (owner: lucas)

lucas: I'll draft the customer follow-up template and share in #support after postmortem.

jen: Scheduling: can we do the postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC? I'll chair and pull in infra and product.

vikram: works for me. will add load test artifacts before the call.

meenakshi: quick monitoring tweaks I'm going to make now:
- Add a short-lived suppression rule for `batcher.flush` to avoid noisy pages during mitigation
- Create composite alert: `embeddings.paging_candidate = p95>2s AND errors>0.5%` before paging
- Add a 3-minute dedupe window for the paging rule

vikram: also propose an SLO clarification: current SLO uses p90 for costing, but p95 is what triggers alerts. We should align SLO target/alerting buckets or at least document the reason for mismatch. (action: record in postmortem)

meenakshi: noted. adding that to postmortem checklist.

incident-bot: BRIDGE CLOSED: embeddings-service incident resolved (duration 00:36). Postmortem required.

lucas: marking customer tickets linked in the incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-ISSUE-2345

jen: I'll open the postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/RED-2345 (draft) and add owners + timeline. Can folks drop short notes there before 12:00 UTC so I can prep the slides?

sara: note for monitoring follow-up: we should add a dashboard widget for `kv_cache_evictions` and `batcher.flush_rate` and set capacity-based baseline so we can see correlation with query throughput.

vikram: creating a small follow-up RFC for safe config rollout (feature flags + gradual TTL change + preflight load test) — will link RFC in postmortem.

meenakshi: thanks team. closing updates here — will sticky action items in the postmortem doc and follow up in the sync. :thumbsup:

jen: thanks everyone. good work on quick rollback and coordinated comms.

sara: resolved for now. I'll reopen if we see anomalies.
